chapter: Records, Blanton, the Chicago scene, Nat Cole and Nadine
title: The Three Deuces quartet with Pearl Bailey and Ann Robinson
summary: On 52nd Street he played with singers Pearl Bailey, Willie Dukes and scat singer Ann Robinson.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: I forgot who was in the quartet. It was at the Three Deuces. Pearl Bailey was singing, and all she

could sing was 'St. Louis Blues.' She was getting 35 dollars a week. And they had a gay young man called Willie Dukes sing Honeysuckle Rose, honey, suck my nose, and Peewee Marquette, you know he couldn't sing.
Was that -- what year was that?
How long had PeeWee been on the scene then? Do you know?
No, I don't. And then they had a girl named Ann Robinson, that could scat like Leo Watson. And she had a big mouth like Martha Raye, only bigger. And she had a nice figure.
Tom Whaley told me about her.
Tom Whaley She worked someplace uptown, right?
Well, she worked at the Village Vanguard for a while. And then she worked at -- what was the name of this place uptown? It was an after hours' spot. I can't think of the name of the place.
Tom described her exactly as you did.

And she ended up getting strangled to death. I don't know how it happened. But she had a secret love. And I can't bare it, because he's my best friend. And he and his wife and living a wonderful life, growing old and

mellow together. I'd hate to bring this up at this late date. That's one of my little goodies that I have to keep to myself. She used to sing 'Chloe' And boy, when she didn't do to "Chloe" -- slush, slush. Now, she would scat. But this is a funny thing. No one in the club made over 35 dollars. Every-place that was working professionally -- 35 dollars.
